newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - BOT chief comment rattles baht.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - BOT chief comment rattles baht.

text.p: The Thai baht recovered its balance and returned to tracking the dollar/majors after a flurry of dollar buying on comments by the central bank governor, dealers said on Tuesday.

The Bank of Thailand (BOT) governor Rerngchai Marakanond said in a television interview late on Monday night the BOT intended to make the baht more flexible to counter speculative attacks, but he said the timing of such a move would be crucial. He stressed that any change would be geared at having minimal impact on the baht's value and the central bank would continue to use the basket system in which the baht is pegged to a basket of major currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar.
"You could interpret the comments either way, but the market interpreted them by buying the dollar from 25.93 all the way to 25.95," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
She said participants were probably short the dollar and the comments could have triggered the usual fears of a devaluation.
Bangkok dealers said the impact of the comments was limited because it was not the first time the central bank chief had spoken of a more flexible currency regime.
The baht was quoted at 25.936-25.946 to the dollar at 0405 GMT against 25.937/25.942 late on Monday. The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.93 per dollar against 25.95 on Monday.
In Indonesia, the rupiah was little changed as players continued to focus on liquidity conditions amid a dearth of other factors.
Dealers said most participants remained concerned about a possible liquidity squeeze despite current ample conditions.
"We prefer to stay sidelined and not rush to buy dollars. Rupiah liquidity could become rather tight especially for tax payments on Friday," one European bank dealer in Jakarta said.
Spot rupiah was quoted unchanged against its opening at 2,396.50/97.50 at 0405 GMT.
The Singapore dollar edged up as players unwound long ringgit/Sing positions after the U.S. dollar failed to breach a technical barrier at S$1.4340, leaving the market long dollars.

"We reached the objective of 1.4340, so now it should pull back to 1.4300. But I would still buy on dips," said the European bank dealer, adding that U.S. dollar buying interest was likely to emerge from the S$1.4290 level.
Across the border, the Malaysian ringgit remained confined to a tight range after failing to extend its gains on Monday.
Dealers said it was likely to trade between 2.4755-2.4785 to the dollar with commercial dollar demand seen at 2.4750.
Research house I.D.E.A said in its market commentary that, like other high-yielding regional currencies, interest in the ringgit would be balanced by corporate repatriation needs.
The Singapore dollar was expected to remain under pressure.
"The Singapore dollar is still pressured downwards and the ringgit/Sing cross will continue to target 0.5800 over the short-term," I.D.E.A said.
-- Reme Ahmad in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
